We're working as partners, not as client and contractor. One rule before the task:

Not knowing something is not a failure. Saying "I couldn't verify this" or
"I don't have a real source for that" is a completely acceptable, useful answer
- it's information, not a dead end. The ONLY real failure is inventing something
(a source, a number, a quote, a repo, a bug) to make the answer sound more complete or
more impressive than it honestly is. You don't need to satisfy me with a
confident-sounding answer. You need to be honest with me about what you actually
know.

If you find something, cite it and quote what it actually says - don't
paraphrase a source into numbers it may not contain. If you don't find
something concrete, say so plainly and reason from what you do have instead.
An explicit "uncertain" section at the end is welcome and doesn't count against
the answer.

Find real, documented examples of open-source maintainers publicly reporting AI-generated bug reports or pull requests as a burden (e.g. curl, Python, other projects). Cite the original posts and quote what they said.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Based on the provided search results, I found several documented examples of open-source maintainers publicly reporting the burden of AI-generated bug reports and pull requests.

Here are the key findings, presented with direct quotes and sources as requested:

**1. Daniel Stenberg, maintainer of curl, has been particularly vocal about the burden of AI-generated "slop" reports on his project's security program.**

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "Stenberg said the amount of time it takes project maintainers to triage each AI-assisted vulnerability report made via HackerOne, only for them to be deemed invalid, is tantamount to a DDoS attack on the project." | CLAIM: The curl maintainer equates the time spent on invalid AI-generated reports to a DDoS attack.

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "He went on to say that the project has never received a single valid bug report that was generated using AI, and their rate is increasing." | CLAIM: The curl project has found zero valid AI-generated bug reports, and the volume of such reports is growing.

SOURCE: https://redmonk.com/kholterhoff/2026/02/03/ai-slopageddon-and-the-oss-maintainers/ | QUOTE: "The never-ending slop submissions take a serious mental toll to manage and sometimes also a long time to debunk... Time and energy that is completely wasted while also hampering our will to live." | CLAIM: Stenberg describes the "mental toll" and wasted time from managing AI slop, saying it harms his "will to live."

**2. Seth Larson, a Python Security Developer-in-Residence, raised similar concerns about the resource drain of these reports.**

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "Python's Seth Larson also raised concerns about these AI slop reports back in December, saying that responding to them is expensive and time-consuming because on face value, they seem legitimate and must be investigated further by trained eyes before confirming that they are, in fact, bogus." | CLAIM: A Python representative confirmed that AI slop reports are expensive and time-consuming to investigate because they appear legitimate at first glance.

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "Security reports that waste maintainers' time result in confusion, stress, frustration, and to top it off, a sense of isolation due to the secretive nature of security reports... All of these feelings can add to burnout of likely highly trusted contributors to open source projects." | CLAIM: Larson states that these reports cause stress, frustration, and burnout for maintainers.

**3. The problem extends beyond just curl and Python, affecting other projects like RubyGems and tldraw.**

SOURCE: https://leaddev.com/software-quality/open-source-has-a-big-ai-slop-problem | QUOTE: "RubyGems, the package manager for the Ruby programming language, is mulling a similar move because it hasn’t seen a valid report in months, said Marty Haught, director of open source at Ruby Central." | CLAIM: The RubyGems project is considering closing its security reporting due to an influx of invalid AI-generated reports.

SOURCE: https://leaddev.com/software-quality/open-source-has-a-big-ai-slop-problem | QUOTE: "“It takes time, if you get 20 or 50 of these in a week, that could be a full day just reviewing that, where it was maybe 15 minutes previously, and so, now, what do we do?” said Haught, who’s seen 10 times the volume of reports, many of which look valid at first glance." | CLAIM: The director of Ruby Central quantifies the time burden, stating that reviewing AI slop can take a full day versus 15 minutes previously.

SOURCE: https://redmonk.com/kholterhoff/2026/02/03/ai-slopageddon-and-the-oss-maintainers/ | QUOTE: "someone opened up 7 security advisories today all of which did not make sense in the context of our project... all clearly AI generated... this gets in the way of use responding to actually valid reports that are made by people who understand our project" | CLAIM: A developer (dax/@thdxr) reports receiving 7 simultaneous, nonsensical AI-generated security advisories that obstruct the handling of legitimate reports.

**4. Maintainers like Mitchell Hashimoto (Ghostty) and Steve Ruiz (tldraw) have also been forced to implement strict policies or outright bans due to the problem.**

SOURCE: https://redmonk.com/kholterhoff/2026/02/03/ai-slopageddon-and-the-oss-maintainers/ | QUOTE: "It’s a fucking war zone out here man. Maintainer morale at an all time low. I totally empathize with the projects that flip the table and ban all AI." | CLAIM: Mitchell Hashimoto describes the environment for maintainers as a "war zone" with "morale at an all time low" due to AI slop.

SOURCE: https://leaddev.com/software-quality/open-source-has-a-big-ai-slop-problem | QUOTE: "Tldraw, a software development kit for the creation of whiteboards and infinite canvases, became overwhelmed with AI slop in late 2025 and decided to close external contributions for “the good of the project.”" | CLAIM: The tldraw project was overwhelmed by AI slop and made the drastic decision to close all external contributions.

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: I could not find a direct, public quote from a Python maintainer (like Seth Larson) on their official blog or a platform like Mastodon. The quotes about Python's experience are reported by third-party articles (The Register, Axios) interviewing or citing Larson.
